newsitem.title: USA: CSCE world sugar called to open little changed.
newsitem.headline: CSCE world sugar called to open little changed.

text.p: CSCE world sugar was called to open mostly unchanged on Friday, dealers said.

They said the heavy open interest in the benchmark October contract makes the market vulnerable to a washout. As of Wednesday, October open interest stood at 108,052 lots, up 2,182 lots from the previous session.
Nearby support remained at 11.40 cents in October followed by 11.25-11.20 cents, resistance was seen at its life-of-contract high set on Tuesday of 11.65 cents.
Thursday, October settled 0.07 cent firmer at 11.56 cents a lb, having ranged from 11.57 to 11.42 cents. The rest of the board finished 0.07 to 0.10 cent higher.
An estimated 14,842 lots changed hands on the day.
On the fundamental side, Ukraine revised down its forecast for the 1997 sugar beet crop to 27 million tonnes from 30-31 million tonnes.
Elsewhere, China imported 360,000 tonnes of sugar in the six months of 1997, down by 35.6 percent from the same period in 1996.
LIFFE white sugar futures were firmer in thin trade Friday. At 0859 EDT/1259 GMT, October was trading 70 cents higher at $328.60.
